items.title: Reese Witherspoon Buys Back Production Firm With Mediawan
items.content: Bloomberg's Chris Palmeri joins Scarlet Fu on "Bloomberg Deals." Actress Reese Witherspoon is repurchasing her film and TV production company Hello Sunshine from Candle Media in partnership with Mediawan, according to a statement from the French entertainment firm. (Source: Bloomberg)

items.title: Starbucks Says It’s Not Buying Chipotle
items.content:
Bloomberg's Daniela Sirtori joins Scarlet Fu on "Bloomberg Deals." Starbucks said it’s not buying Chipotle Mexican Grill, tamping down speculation about what could have been one of the restaurant sector’s largest-ever deals.
 (Source: Bloomberg)

items.title: Bumble Said to Near $1B Sale to Ithaca
items.content: Bloomberg's Liana Baker joins Scarlet Fu on "Bloomberg Deals." Dating-app provider Bumble is in talks to be sold to upstart investment firm Ithaca Holdings for around $1 billion, according to people familiar with the matter. (Source: Bloomberg)

items.title: BofA Takes US Regulatory Fines Seriously, CEO Moynihan Says
items.content: Bank of America Corp. Chief Executive Officer Brian Moynihan addresses the $1.2 billion in fines levied against the company by the US government. He says the bank takes the fines seriously and there is accountability at the firm. He says costs associated with these fines are in the company "baseline." He speaks to Bloomberg's Jonathan Ferro. (Source: Bloomberg)

items.title: Economy Overshadows GOP Border Success, Says Samara Klar
items.content: Samara Klar, professor at the University of Arizona School of Government and Public Policy, said that high prices are dragging Republican messaging in Arizona ahead of President Trump's visit to campaign in the state. Klar also spoke about the how the issue of immigration enforcement and border security is playing alongside affordability. She said that Republicans might not be able to capitalize on border wins as 'the economy is such an issue for voters that in many ways it’s overshadowing a lot of the successes Republicans might have otherwise been able to claim when it comes to border security.' (Source: Bloomberg)

items.title: NYC Transit Agency Cuts Bond Refinancing 40% Amid Yield Spike
items.content: The Metropolitan Transportation Authority, which operates New York City’s subways, buses and commuter lines, cut a planned debt refinancing by about 40% as tax-exempt bond yields hovered near their highest levels in at least 15 years.
